title: A compatible horizontal Cartier boundary for a descended affine open
statement: Let $B\to C$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism of discrete valuation rings, and put $K=\operatorname{Frac}B$, $L=\operatorname{Frac}C$ (their localizations at nonzero elements), $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $S'=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X'\to S'$ be smooth separated of finite type, with descent datum $\alpha$ relative to $S'/S$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-pd-descent-datum]. Separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose the generic datum is realized by a $K$-scheme $X_0$ with $X_0\times_KL\simeq X'_L$ [def-pc-base-change]. Let $U\to S$ be affine, and suppose an isomorphism $U\times_SS'\simeq U'\subseteq X'$ realizes the restricted datum on an invariant affine open $U'$ dense in every geometric fibre [def-weil-open-immersion]. Require also an open immersion $U_K\hookrightarrow X_0$ inducing $U'_L\hookrightarrow X'_L$. Then there is an effective Cartier divisor $D_0\subseteq X_0$ with support $X_0\setminus U_K$. Its schematic closure $D'$ in $X'$ is an effective Cartier divisor with support $X'\setminus U'$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal, def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. Schematic closure here means the closed subscheme with ideal $\ker(\mathcal O_{X'}\to j_*\mathcal O_{(D_0)_L})$, where $j:(D_0)_L\to X'$ is the composite inclusion. Over $S'\times_SS'$, the datum identifies the two pulled-back closed subschemes $p_0^*D'$ and $p_1^*D'$. It consequently gives an isomorphism between the pullbacks of the invertible module $\mathcal O_{X'}(D')$ satisfying the same cocycle as $\alpha$ [def-sc-invertible-module, def-pc-module-pullback]. The empty divisor is permitted. No group structure or ampleness is asserted.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Theorem 1 proof, case (a), printed p.160 (PDF p.166): choose the generic boundary divisor and close it in the smooth trait scheme; schematic closure and flat pullback give the datum on the divisor and its associated line. EGA IV4, 21.12.7 supplies the generic boundary divisor. Local BLR PDF WANTED; primary scan read online.

proof.text: Choose uniformizers $\pi_B,\pi_C$. A DVR is Noetherian since its ideals are principal. Its dimension is one by [lem-sc-dvr-dimension-one], so its principal maximal ideal makes it regular local; its only other prime is $(0)$, whose localization is its fraction field, regular of dimension zero. Thus $B,C,K,L$ are regular rings. The map $B\to C$ is injective: $C$ is flat over the domain $B$, hence torsion-free, and $1_C\ne0$. Surjectivity on spectra gives a prime of $C$ above the nonzero maximal ideal of $B$; it must be the maximal ideal of $C$. Thus the image of $\pi_B$ is a nonzero nonunit. The DVR power theorem writes it as $u\pi_C^e$ with $e\ge1$. Consequently $C\otimes_BK=C[1/\pi_B]=C[1/\pi_C]=L$. Also $X'_L$ is the principal open where $\pi_C$ is invertible, by principal localization and open-immersion base change.

source.place: Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr); Tag 00IE; localization at a uniformizer.

proof.text: Every point of $X'$ has a smooth affine neighbourhood over an affine open of $\operatorname{Spec}C$. Such a nonempty base open is either $\operatorname{Spec}C$ or $\operatorname{Spec}L$. Smooth restriction and the affine smoothness equivalence turn these into smooth ring maps from $C$ or $L$. Regularity ascends along those maps, so the affine coordinate rings are regular and Noetherian. Stalk localization shows that every local ring of $X'$ is regular local. Finite type over the affine base gives quasi-compactness, so $X'$ is Noetherian. The regular-local UFD theorem, with the empty parameter list, makes all its stalks UFDs. Smoothness also makes $X'\to S'$ flat. At a point of the special fibre its stalk is flat over $C$, so $\pi_C$ is nonzero there by torsion-freeness. At a point of the generic fibre it is a unit. These observations will exclude vertical generic points. Finally $X'$ is an absolutely separated scheme by the separated-over-affine lemma.

source.place: Tag 036D (lemma-regular-local-smooth), ascent; Algebra Tag 07NF; More on Algebra Tag 0AG0 (lemma-regular-local-UFD).

proof.text: The morphism $X'_L\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is smooth, separated and finite type by the smooth, separated, locally-finite-type and quasi-compact base-change statements. The field cover $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is fpqc. Apply smoothness, separatedness, local finite type and quasi-compact fpqc descent to the already given $X_0$. It follows that $X_0$ is smooth separated finite type over $K$. It is regular and locally Noetherian by smooth-field regularity, and quasi-compact by finite type, hence Noetherian. Regular-normal decomposition writes it as a finite disjoint union of integral open-and-closed schemes $X_i$. Density of $U'_L$ in the ordinary generic fibre follows from density after algebraic closure: a nonempty open stays nonempty after field extension by faithful flatness and spectrum surjectivity. A nonempty $X_i$ meets $U_K$: otherwise its nonempty pullback to $L$ would be an open disjoint from the dense $U'_L$. Nonemptiness and this density test can be checked on affine spectra using faithful flatness of field scalar extension and surjectivity on spectra.

source.place: Tags 02VL, 02KU, 02KX, 02KQ; Varieties Tag 056S; Properties Tags 0569 and 033M.

proof.text: The scheme $U_K$ is affine by affine-morphism base change from $U\to S$ and affine permanence. Put $U_i=U_K\cap X_i$. It is a nonempty affine open of $X_i$: it is open and closed in $U_K$, and is the closed subscheme whose ideal is zero on $U_i$ and the unit ideal on its open complement. It is therefore affine by closed-immersion affineness and affine permanence. The restrictions $X_i\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ are smooth, and are separated finite type because they are open-and-closed pieces of the Noetherian $X_0$. Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-affine-cartier-boundary] to each $X_i,U_i$. On the finite disjoint union define $D_0$ by these divisor ideals on its open-and-closed pieces. There are no overlaps between distinct pieces, so these ideals define a Cartier divisor, with support $X_0\setminus U_K$. If $X_0$ is empty the same prescription gives the empty divisor. Pullback to $L$ is Cartier by flat Cartier pullback; call the resulting divisor $E\subset X'_L$. Its support is $X'_L\setminus U'_L$: the complement of a closed subscheme pulls back to the complement of its inverse-image closed subscheme, as is immediate from the local ideal equations.

source.place: Tag 0BCW (lemma-complement-open-affine-effective-cartier-divisor), componentwise; Tag 02OO (6), flat Cartier pullback.

proof.text: Let $g:E\to X'$ be the inclusion through the generic open. It is quasi-compact: over an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X'$, its inverse image is a closed subscheme of the principal affine open $W[1/\pi_C]$, hence affine. Thus $g$ is affine and therefore quasi-compact. Define $D'=\operatorname{SIm}(g)$. The quasi-compact scheme-image kernel statement identifies its ideal with $\ker(\mathcal O_{X'}\to g_*\mathcal O_E)$, exactly the closure requested in the statement. The image-support statement gives $|D'|=\overline{|E|}$. Flat image base change to the generic open, followed by the image-of-closed-immersion statement, gives $D'\cap X'_L=E$ as closed subschemes. In particular multiplicities have not been discarded.

source.place: Tags 01R8, 01RA, 081I (lemma-flat-base-change-scheme-theoretic-image); the principal open is localization at the uniformizer.

proof.text: The factorial-complement extension theorem applies to $X'_L\subset X'$ and $E$: step 2 gives local Noetherianity and UFD stalks on the complement. Choose an effective Cartier divisor $H\subset X'$ restricting to $E$. This theorem asserts only an extension; it does not identify that extension with the schematic closure. Fix $x\in X'$ and put $A=\mathcal O_{X',x}$ and $a=\pi_C\in A$. The canonical local-spectrum morphism $c:\operatorname{Spec}A\to X'$ is flat. Pulling the image $D'$ back along $c$ is therefore the scheme-theoretic image of $E\times_{X'}\operatorname{Spec}A$. If $h\in A$ is a local Cartier equation of $H$ at $x$, this source is the closed subscheme defined by $h$ in $\operatorname{Spec}A[1/a]$. Here $h\ne0$ since it is a nonzerodivisor in the domain $A$, and $a\ne0$ by step 2. The kernel formula gives its image ideal as $J=\{b\in A:\exists n\ge0,\ a^nb\in(h)\}$.

source.place: Tag 0BD8 (lemma-closure-effective-cartier-divisor), closure construction and local reduction; Morphisms Tag 081I.

proof.text: Factor $h$ in the UFD $A$ and let $h_0$ be the product, with the same exponents, of precisely those prime factors of $h$ which do not divide $a$; the product may be $1$. Then $J=(h_0)$. Indeed $a^nb\in(h)$ forces every retained prime power to divide $b$, since its prime does not divide $a$; conversely, if $h_0\mid b$, a sufficiently large power of $a$ supplies all the deleted prime powers, giving $h\mid a^nb$. Thus $J$ is generated by the nonzero element $h_0$, a nonzerodivisor. The canonical local-spectrum stalk identification makes $J$ the stalk ideal of $D'$ at $x$. This holds at every $x$. Apply the stalk-nonzerodivisor Cartier spreading theorem to the closed subscheme $D'$ of the locally Noetherian $X'$; it proves that $D'$ is an effective Cartier divisor. This saturation computation, rather than the arbitrary extension $H$, is what proves Cartierness of the specified schematic closure.

source.place: Tag 0BD8, proof, prime-power equation for the closure; Tag 0AG8 (lemma-effective-Cartier-in-points).

proof.text: The open $U'$ is dense in $X'$. To see this, each irreducible component of the regular Noetherian $X'$ is open and closed by regular-normal decomposition. At its generic point the local ring is a field. Step 2 says $\pi_C$ is nonzero there, hence a unit, so this component meets $X'_L$. Its generic open consequently meets $U'_L$, which is dense by hypothesis, and therefore $U'$ meets every component and is dense. The same hypothesis gives density of $U'$ in the ordinary special fibre: if a nonempty fibre open missed $U'$, its pullback to an algebraic closure of the residue field would be nonempty by field-extension faithful flatness and spectrum surjectivity, contradicting geometric-fibre density. No special fibre is required to be nonempty.

source.place: Tag 0BCV, density hypothesis; BLR 6.5 Theorem 1, case (a), fibrewise density of the chosen affine open.

proof.text: Write $Z=X'\setminus U'$. The affine-boundary codimension theorem applies since $X'$ is absolutely separated and locally Noetherian and $U'$ is dense affine. Each generic point $\xi$ of a component of $Z$ has $\dim\mathcal O_{X',\xi}=1$. Such points exist by sobriety of schemes. None is in the special fibre: if it were, the dimension-one local domain $A=\mathcal O_{X',\xi}$ would contain the nonzero $\pi_C$ in its maximal ideal. Its only primes are $(0)$ and the maximal ideal, so no strictly smaller prime contains $\pi_C$. By the local-spectrum generalization correspondence, $\xi$ would then be a generic point of an irreducible component of the special fibre. A dense open in that fibre must contain this point, contrary to $\xi\in Z$. Hence every component of $Z$ has its generic point in $Z\cap X'_L=|E|$. Thus $Z=\overline{|E|}$: one inclusion follows since $Z$ is closed and contains $|E|$, the other by taking closures of these generic points. Step 5 now gives $|D'|=Z$. This also handles $Z=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0BCV (lemma-complement-affine-open); the horizontal-support argument in BLR 6.5 Theorem 1, printed pp.160-161.

proof.text: Put $T=S'\times_SS'$ and let $Y_i=X'\times_{S',p_i}T$ with projection $q_i:Y_i\to X'$. These projections are flat: over $W=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset X'$, they are the maps on spectra of $R\to R\otimes_B C$ (with the appropriate $C$ factor), which are faithfully flat by faithfully-flat ring base change and flat by the affine criterion. Apply flat scheme-image base change to $g:E\to X'$ along each $q_i$. It identifies $q_i^*D'$ with the scheme-theoretic image of the corresponding pullback of $E$. Over $T_K$, those two pullbacks of $E=(D_0)_L$ are identified by $\alpha$, since the generic datum is the one induced by the specified model $X_0$ and $D_0$ is a closed subscheme of that model. They are empty off $T_K$ as source schemes. Under $\alpha:Y_0\simeq Y_1$, the two source morphisms into $Y_i$ therefore agree. Their kernel ideals and scheme-theoretic images agree. Hence $\alpha$ identifies $q_0^*D'$ and $q_1^*D'$ as closed subschemes over all of $T$, including their multiplicities.

source.place: Tag 081I; BLR 6.5 Theorem 1, case (a), printed p.160, equality of the two pulled-back divisors.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the Cartier ideal of $D'$ and put $M'=I^\vee=\mathcal O_{X'}(D')$. It is invertible by the divisor-line invertibility theorem. Flat Cartier pullback identifies $q_i^*I$ with the ideal of $q_i^*D'$. The identification in step 10 induces an isomorphism between these ideals along $\alpha$. Dualizing its inverse gives the required forward isomorphism on their associated lines, using divisor-line flat pullback. The comparisons can be chosen canonically: for a ring map $A\to R$ and a free rank-one ideal $I=(h)$, the map $R\otimes_A I^\vee\to(R\otimes_AI)^\vee$ sends $b\otimes\lambda$ to $(c\otimes s\mapsto bc\lambda(s))$. On the frame $h$ it is an isomorphism. This formula is independent of the frame (replacing $h$ by $uh$ replaces the dual frame by $u^{-1}$), and so glues. It also commutes with successive scalar extension and with isomorphisms of ideals, directly by its displayed formula. Thus this construction gives a datum on the specified line itself.

source.place: Tag 0C4U (lemma-pullback-effective-Cartier-divisors); Tag 02OO (6); definition of the divisor line as the dual ideal.

proof.text: On $S'\times_SS'\times_SS'$, the two composites of the induced ideal maps are equal: they are the restrictions of the maps of structure sheaves induced by the two equal composites in the cocycle for $\alpha$. Taking the dual of the inverse preserves this equality and its direction. The scalar-extension comparisons of step 11 commute with composition by the displayed tensor formula, so the line isomorphism satisfies precisely the same cocycle. The identity-cover and empty-divisor cases give respectively the identity construction and the usual datum on $\mathcal O_{X'}$. This completes every asserted clause; no group law or positivity input has entered.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q106-e4750b057 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 12 steps and every cited statement. The delivery is one commit with no new nodes, and the statement and stmt_deps are verbatim the live unsplit node. Steps 6-7 follow the proof of Stacks 0BD8 (divisors.tex l.7093, read), with the local equation made explicit: J={b : a^n b∈(h)}=(h_0), where h_0 drops the prime factors of h that divide π_C. I checked both inclusions in the UFD. Stalk spreading then makes the prescribed closure D' Cartier; H from the extension node only supplies h. Steps 5 and 10 use flat scheme-image base change (081I, morphisms.tex l.4965, read). The q_i are flat on charts R→R⊗_B C. The preimage of X'_L is the part over T_K, because inverting π_C is the same as inverting π_B. So α identifies q_0^*D' and q_1^*D' as closed subschemes. Step 9: a codim-1 generic point of the boundary that lay in the special fibre would be a generic point of a component of X'_s, which contradicts fibrewise density; so the support is X'∖U'. Every hypothesis of the cited nodes checks: affine-boundary codim (separated, locally Noetherian, dense affine), smooth-affine-cartier-boundary on the integral components, and fpqc descent along Spec L→Spec K. I tested A^1⊃G_m, U'=X', an empty special fibre and ramified e>1. Batch 5: lem-trf-flat-module-torsionfree-domain (0539), lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization (0AG0), lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent (02VL) and lem-trf-ufd-height-one (0AFT), reached through the two sfb nodes, are generic commutative-algebra and descent lemmas. Neither the trace formula nor Poincaré duality gives them, and none is a step of their proofs, so all are accepted. I accept the declared tool_uses: generic leaves and lemmas used as black boxes. No SGA is cited.
